question: How can a VLM agent understand temporal information in video while reducing video-reading tokens?

operations.query: long video multimodal agent temporal grounding token efficient frame selection

evidence.title: LongVT: Thinking with Long Videos via Native Tool Calling
evidence.excerpt: The official README describes a global-to-local loop: skim globally, use temporal grounding as a crop tool, then resample finer-grained frames in a relevant clip.

evidence.title: LongVideoAgent: Multi-Agent Reasoning with Long Videos
evidence.excerpt: The official repository describes a bounded master-agent loop coordinating a grounding agent to locate relevant segments and a vision agent to inspect targeted visual details.
evidence.locator: README abstract and iterative reasoning loop

evidence.title: M-LLM Based Video Frame Selection for Efficient Video Understanding
evidence.excerpt: The paper reports query-aware spatial and temporal frame selection, using captions for temporal reasoning and showing selected frames can outperform twice as many uniformly sampled frames on long-video benchmarks.

evidence.title: VideoITG: Instructed Temporal Grounding
evidence.excerpt: The official evaluation pipeline writes per-frame grounding scores and selects K frames for a downstream VLM, making the grounding-to-reading boundary explicit.

evidence.title: X discussion: StreamingVLM and long-video attention sinks
evidence.excerpt: A researcher discussion describes long-video systems as million-token contexts and presents attention sinks plus sliding windows as a way to preserve a global prior. This is a useful frontier signal, not independent benchmark evidence.

evidence.title: Reddit discussion: temporal grounding remains an open problem
evidence.excerpt: A visible comment argues that long-video systems still struggle to keep precise temporal grounding while compressing frames. It is a community observation and not a technical validation.

evidence.title: Bilibili: Qwen3-VL technical report discussion
evidence.excerpt: The visible page description discusses long-context video, timestamp alignment, and temporal event localization. The video itself was not downloaded or transcribed in this run.

claims.text: The most defensible implementation pattern is a bounded global-to-local loop: use ASR/captions or a low-cost temporal scan to locate candidate intervals, then inspect only those intervals with dense frames and a VLM.
claims.confidenceReason: Independent official repositories and a paper converge on temporal grounding, targeted frame selection, and bounded iterative inspection.

claims.text: Token reduction should happen before the expensive VLM pass: captions/ASR and frame scores can rank candidate moments, while the downstream VLM receives a small timestamped evidence set instead of the full video.
claims.confidenceReason: The paper gives query-aware selection results, and the repositories expose explicit grounding-to-K-frame pipelines.

claims.text: Social discussion is useful for discovering unresolved issues such as preserving a stable timeline under compression, but it should not establish the technical result by itself.
claims.confidenceReason: The visible X and Reddit materials agree on the concern, but both are secondary and incomplete.

claims.text: This run verifies page-level discovery of a Bilibili video, but does not verify its audiovisual content, ASR quality, visual observations, or comments.
claims.confidenceReason: The media runtime and authenticated/session-bound reading tools were unavailable during this run.

limitations: This is a live web research run, not a private BrowserOS/Whisper/VLM execution.
No raw cookies, provider keys, or private media were accessed.
Bilibili was read only at page-snippet level; no ASR, frame understanding, or comment reading is claimed.
X and Reddit evidence is secondary discovery/community evidence and does not outrank official code or papers.
